title: Operational acceptance and network fallback checklist for Private VPC deployments
creator: Amina Khatri
description:
Purpose: Define the operational requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout checks for Private (VPC / air-gapped) deployments centered on networking constraints and offline upgrade flows. This PRD clarifies scope compared to existing networking/upgrades tickets: focus is on runtime operational readiness (fallbacks, validation probes, observable signals) rather than implementation design of the upgrade service itself. Scope includes: ingress/egress policy matrix, image/package delivery & verification for air-gapped installs, pre-upgrade validation tasks, post-upgrade confirmation criteria, and explicit rollback triggers. Out of scope: upstream compiler/kernel selection logic and hosted API rate-limiting behaviour.

Rationale: Teams running Redwood Private must be able to perform upgrades and recoveries in restrictive networks with high confidence. We need a machine-readable checklist and deterministic acceptance gates so ops engineers can validate upgrades in customer-controlled networks and so automated playbooks can run in air-gapped contexts.
acceptance_criteria: Network policy matrix documented: required outbound destinations (IP ranges/FQDNs), ports, and protocols for 'full-connect' and 'restricted' modes; clearly labelled which destinations are mandatory vs optional for telemetry/metrics. Example: container registry (signed image retrieval) is mandatory for online upgrades; metrics-forwarder endpoint is optional if offline-metrics-bundle provided.

Offline upgrade bundle spec: a deterministic tarball format (manifest.json + signed images + dependency list) validated against a documented signing scheme (SHA256 + vendor-signature) and sample verification CLI; verification returns non-zero on mismatch.

Image signing and provenance: every runtime image and operator bundle used during upgrades MUST be signed. Acceptance requires demonstration of signature verification in an air-gapped lab (no external DNS/HTTP).

KMS integration test: customer-managed KMS/HSM flows validated during pre-upgrade and post-upgrade steps. Acceptance requires ability to rotate a key and confirm all node agents reconnect using the updated key without data loss or credential leakage.

Upgrade dry-run validation: a preflight step runs in-customer-cluster, checks resource availability (CPU/memory/GPU), PV accessibility, network policies, and returns a machine-readable report with pass/warn/fail for each check.

Canary and fallback behaviour: deploy a canary to 5% of nodes (configurable). If canary health < 99% for 3 consecutive minutes or error rate increases by > 5x baseline, automated rollback must trigger and notify configured webhook/Slack channel. Acceptance requires a simulated canary failure in staging that demonstrates rollback and clear audit logs of the decision path.

Health and observability signals: define and document the set of minimum health metrics (control-plane-heartbeat, runtime-kv-cache-miss-rate, token-serve-latency P95/P99, process-crash-count) that must be emitted during upgrade. Acceptance requires dashboards for these metrics and at least one alert rule with runbook link configured.

Maintenance window mechanics: upgrades initiated outside maintenance windows must be blocked by default. Tickets that override must include justification and recorded approver. Acceptance requires policy enforcement in the upgrade controller and an audit trail entry for manual overrides.

Rollback verification: after rollback, cluster must confirm previous model version and runtime configuration within 5 minutes and serve traffic at pre-upgrade latency baselines within 30 minutes. Acceptance requires post-rollback smoke tests passing in a staged lab environment.

Documentation and operator checklist: an operator-facing checklist (printable) for offline upgrades including preflight commands, expected outputs, troubleshooting hints, and escalation contacts. Acceptance requires review and sign-off by Solutions Engineering and Support on the checklist content.
test_plan: Air-gapped installation simulation: perform a full install/upgrade in an isolated lab with no egress; validate bundle verification, signature checks, and runtime startup logs.

Network-restricted scenario: block optional telemetry endpoints and validate that core serving remains operational; confirm warnings generated but upgrade proceeds only when mandatory endpoints reachable (unless offline bundle used).
Canary failure injection: in staging, intentionally corrupt canary image to trigger health degradation and verify automated rollback, alerting, and audit logs.
Key rotation and KMS failover test: rotate customer-managed key in lab and force KMS latency; validate that agents retry, drain, and re-establish secure channels without secret exposure.
Metrics and alerting validation: trigger synthetic spikes in token-serve-latency and ensure alerts fire and runbook steps reproduce the investigation flow.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Docs & bundles: publish offline bundle spec, verification CLI, and operator checklist to private-deploy docs site.
Phase 1 - Staging validation: run full test_plan in staging cluster replicating restricted networking; sign-off from SE and SRE required.
Phase 2 - Pilot customers: run upgrades for 2 pilot customers (restricted and air-gapped) with dedicated SE support; collect telemetry and post-upgrade report.
Phase 3 - Gradual rollout: enable automated canary at 5%, then 25%, then 100% with 24-hr observation windows and rollback gates at each step.
Phase 4 - GA: publish release notes, operator checklist, and enable default enforcement of maintenance window and signature checks.
notes: This ticket synthesizes acceptance criteria across prior network/airgap tickets but focuses on operational checks and observable gates required to safely run upgrades in customer-controlled networks. Coordinate with Security for signing scheme and with Engineering for controller enforcement behaviors. Schedule a tabletop run with Support and SE before Pilot stage.
